lines.text: Which ashwagandha brand is actually worth buying in 2026? We read six US labels, line by line. Here is what we found.
lines.say: Which ashwagandha brand is actually worth buying in twenty twenty-six? We read six U S labels, line by line. Here is what we found.

lines.text: The short answer. Buy the extract, not the brand. Look for a named root extract, at 300 to 600 milligrams a day, with nothing hidden.
lines.say: The short answer. Buy the extract, not the brand. Look for a named root extract, at three hundred to six hundred milligrams a day, with nothing hidden.

lines.text: How we chose. The trials behind ashwagandha for stress and sleep mostly used 250 to 600 milligrams a day of a standardised root extract, for eight weeks. Several used one called KSM-66.
lines.say: How we chose. The trials behind ashwagandha for stress and sleep mostly used two hundred and fifty to six hundred milligrams a day of a standardised root extract, for eight weeks. Several used one called K S M sixty-six.

lines.text: For each product, we read the Supplement Facts panel on the maker's own website, on the 1st of October, and worked out the daily dose and the cost a day. We did not test the capsules ourselves.
lines.say: For each product, we read the Supplement Facts panel on the maker's own website, on the first of October, and worked out the daily dose and the cost a day. We did not test the capsules ourselves.

lines.text: Which extract? KSM-66 is the best studied, a root only extract used in many of the stress, sleep and strength trials. Sensoril is also trial tested, more concentrated and dosed lower. Plain root powder is much weaker per capsule.
lines.say: Which extract? K S M sixty-six is the best studied, a root only extract used in many of the stress, sleep and strength trials. Sensoril is also trial tested, more concentrated and dosed lower. Plain root powder is much weaker per capsule.

lines.text: Our top pick is NOW KSM-66 Ashwagandha, 600 milligrams. One capsule a day gives the extract, and the dose, that did best in the trials. At the list price it costs about 37 cents a day, and one bottle lasts three months. The catch: the withanolide percentage is not printed on the label.
lines.say: Our top pick is Now K S M sixty-six Ashwagandha, six hundred milligrams. One capsule a day gives the extract, and the dose, that did best in the trials. At the list price it costs about thirty-seven cents a day, and one bottle lasts three months. The catch: the withanolide percentage is not printed on the label.

lines.text: For a split dose, Jarrow Formulas Ashwagandha, 300 milligrams. It is KSM-66 again, one capsule twice a day, the same pattern as the best known stress trial. About 42 cents a day. Some listings still call it Sensoril, so check the label on your bottle.
lines.say: For a split dose, Jarrow Formulas Ashwagandha, three hundred milligrams. It is K S M sixty-six again, one capsule twice a day, the same pattern as the best known stress trial. About forty-two cents a day. Some listings still call it Sensoril, so check the label on your bottle.

lines.text: On a budget, NOW Ashwagandha 450. About 19 cents a day, with the withanolide content printed on the label. But it is a generic root and leaf extract, not one of the extracts the trials tested.
lines.say: On a budget, Now Ashwagandha four fifty. About nineteen cents a day, with the withanolide content printed on the label. But it is a generic root and leaf extract, not one of the extracts the trials tested.

lines.text: To start low, Life Extension Optimized Ashwagandha. It uses Sensoril, a more concentrated extract that was studied at smaller doses. This is 250 milligrams a day. The price is hidden until you sign in.
lines.say: To start low, Life Extension Optimized Ashwagandha. It uses Sensoril, a more concentrated extract that was studied at smaller doses. This is two hundred and fifty milligrams a day. The price is hidden until you sign in.

lines.text: If you prefer whole root, Gaia Herbs Ashwagandha Root is organic, and honest about its strength. But each capsule has 2.5 milligrams of withanolides, about a twelfth of a 600 milligram KSM-66 capsule.
lines.say: If you prefer whole root, Gaia Herbs Ashwagandha Root is organic, and honest about its strength. But each capsule has two and a half milligrams of withanolides, about a twelfth of a six hundred milligram K S M sixty-six capsule.

lines.text: And if you want a gummy, Goli does use KSM-66. But the full dose is four gummies a day. That is 8 grams of sugar, 2,000 IU of vitamin D, and about $1.67 a day. Four times the cost of the capsules.
lines.say: And if you want a gummy, Goli does use K S M sixty-six. But the full dose is four gummies a day. That is eight grams of sugar, two thousand I U of vitamin D, and about a dollar sixty-seven a day. Four times the cost of the capsules.

lines.chapter: Cost a day, side by side
lines.text: Side by side, at list price. 19 cents a day for the budget pick. 37 for our top pick. 42 for Jarrow. And $1.67 for the gummies.
lines.say: Side by side, at list price. Nineteen cents a day for the budget pick. Thirty-seven for our top pick. Forty-two for Jarrow. And a dollar sixty-seven for the gummies.

lines.text: One thing to remember. A higher milligram number is not a stronger product. Compare the extract and the withanolides, not the big number on the front.
lines.say: One thing to remember. A higher milligram number is not a stronger product. Compare the extract and the withanolides, not the big number on the front.

lines.chapter: What to check on any label
lines.text: What to check on any label. A named extract, or a withanolide percentage. 250 to 600 milligrams of extract a day. Root, rather than leaf. No proprietary blend hiding the amount. And clear warnings about pregnancy, thyroid and liver conditions.
lines.say: What to check on any label. A named extract, or a withanolide percentage. Two hundred and fifty to six hundred milligrams of extract a day. Root, rather than leaf. No proprietary blend hiding the amount. And clear warnings about pregnancy, thyroid and liver conditions.

lines.text: Is organic better? Organic describes how the plant was grown, not how strong the product is. Check the extract and the dose first.
lines.say: Is organic better? Organic describes how the plant was grown, not how strong the product is. Check the extract and the dose first.

lines.text: What to avoid. Proprietary blends, which do not tell you how much ashwagandha you are taking. And stacked formulas that add melatonin, magnesium or L-theanine. Then you are taking a mixture.
lines.say: What to avoid. Proprietary blends, which do not tell you how much ashwagandha you are taking. And stacked formulas that add melatonin, magnesium or L-theanine. Then you are taking a mixture.

lines.text: Be wary of megadose claims. A capsule advertising 1,000 milligrams or more is often root powder, or a less concentrated extract. And clinically proven on the front only counts if the label matches the trials.
lines.say: Be wary of megadose claims. A capsule advertising a thousand milligrams or more is often root powder, or a less concentrated extract. And clinically proven on the front only counts if the label matches the trials.

lines.text: Before you buy any brand. Do not take ashwagandha if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Check with your doctor first if you have a thyroid or liver condition, an autoimmune disease, or take regular medicines.
lines.say: Before you buy any brand. Do not take ashwagandha if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Check with your doctor first if you have a thyroid or liver condition, an autoimmune disease, or take regular medicines.

lines.text: Rare liver injury has been reported, usually 2 to 12 weeks after starting. So plan an eight week trial, and stop by about three months.
lines.say: Rare liver injury has been reported, usually two to twelve weeks after starting. So plan an eight week trial, and stop by about three months.

lines.text: The bottom line. For most people: NOW KSM-66, one capsule a day. For a split dose: Jarrow. On a budget: NOW 450. Compare the cost a day, not the price of the bottle. This is general information, not medical advice. The full guide is at sharpandlean.com.
